questions.q: A Hadith calls differences of opinion “a mercy.” What one condition does the editorial set for expressing them?
options: They should be settled by a vote
Not quite. The article says: They should rest on accepted evidence, without allegations against the other person.
They should be kept private
Not quite. The article says: They should rest on accepted evidence, without allegations against the other person.
They should rest on accepted evidence, without allegations against the other person
Yes. Then they bring new aspects of a subject to light.
They should be voiced only by scholars
Not quite. The article says: They should rest on accepted evidence, without allegations against the other person.
questions.rationale: “Those who disagree with each other should do so on the basis of accepted evidence and must abstain from hurling allegations against others.”

questions.article: Peace for the Sake of Peace
questions.q: The article compares peace to rain. What is the point?
options: Rain only waters the field; the farmer must sow and work – peace gives opportunity, not the goal itself
Right. Hence “peace for the sake of peace.”
Too much peace, like too much rain, does harm
Not quite. The article says: Rain only waters the field; the farmer must sow and work – peace gives opportunity, not the goal itself.
Peace, like rain, cannot be predicted
Not quite. The article says: Rain only waters the field; the farmer must sow and work – peace gives opportunity, not the goal itself.
Peace, like rain, comes only in season
Not quite. The article says: Rain only waters the field; the farmer must sow and work – peace gives opportunity, not the goal itself.
questions.rationale: “Peace is like rain. Peace only provides you with opportunities. It is upon people to avail these opportunities through wise planning.”

questions.q: How does the article reconcile equality between men and women with the fact that they often do different work?
options: Equality of status goes together with a division of labour based on ability
Yes. Such differences exist between any two people.
Equality means everyone must do the same tasks
Not quite. The article says: Equality of status goes together with a division of labour based on ability.
Work should be assigned by age
Not quite. The article says: Equality of status goes together with a division of labour based on ability.
Different work shows that equality is impossible
Not quite. The article says: Equality of status goes together with a division of labour based on ability.
questions.rationale: “The formula should be ‘Gender equality while maintaining division of labour’… division is based on ability and not on gender.”

questions.q: What does the article recommend as the practical way to secure women’s equal standing in society?
options: Reserving half of all posts
Not quite. The article says: Giving girls quality education and training.
Holding public campaigns
Not quite. The article says: Giving girls quality education and training.
Passing more laws
Not quite. The article says: Giving girls quality education and training.
Giving girls quality education and training
Correct. Then equal status follows “without making any formal demands.”
questions.rationale: “We need to provide quality education to girls, give them the best training… women will be able to attain an equal status in society.”

questions.article: The Answer Is Very Much Here
questions.q: For centuries people held that the sun went round the earth. Why does the article recall this?
options: To praise the scholars of the ancient world
Not quite. The article says: To show how a fixed way of looking can keep people from seeing an answer that is already there.
To show that science is often wrong
Not quite. The article says: To show how a fixed way of looking can keep people from seeing an answer that is already there.
To prove that the earth is unimportant
Not quite. The article says: To show how a fixed way of looking can keep people from seeing an answer that is already there.
To show how a fixed way of looking can keep people from seeing an answer that is already there
Well reasoned. Here the fixed idea is “right here, right now.”
questions.rationale: “People are obsessed with wrong ideas… It is this difference in outlook between the reader and the book that has created the problem.”

questions.q: What precedent does the article see in Adam’s removal from Paradise?
options: Paradise, once lost, cannot be regained
Not quite. The article says: Paradise is earned by one’s deeds and self-restraint; it is no one’s birthright.
Paradise is earned by one’s deeds and self-restraint; it is no one’s birthright
Yes. Not even for the Prophets.
Paradise is reserved for Adam’s descendants
Not quite. The article says: Paradise is earned by one’s deeds and self-restraint; it is no one’s birthright.
Paradise was only a symbol
Not quite. The article says: Paradise is earned by one’s deeds and self-restraint; it is no one’s birthright.
questions.rationale: “No one will be given Paradise magically or on the basis of recommendations from anyone. Paradise is not a birth-right even for the Prophets.”

questions.q: By what measure, says the article, should a “big” achievement be judged?
options: How dangerous it was
Not quite. The article says: Whether it is of real benefit to people, not whether it brings personal glory.
How much it cost
Not quite. The article says: Whether it is of real benefit to people, not whether it brings personal glory.
Whether it is of real benefit to people, not whether it brings personal glory
Right. Marie Curie and Helen Keller are the examples.
How widely it was reported
Not quite. The article says: Whether it is of real benefit to people, not whether it brings personal glory.
questions.rationale: “Big dreams must be creative and beneficial for humanity. They should not merely be a source of sensational news and personal glory.”

questions.q: What sign does the article look for in someone who has truly found God?
options: Long speeches about religion
Not quite. The article says: An inner life visibly touched and changed – not just claims and public fervour.
Many followers
Not quite. The article says: An inner life visibly touched and changed – not just claims and public fervour.
Wealth and success
Not quite. The article says: An inner life visibly touched and changed – not just claims and public fervour.
An inner life visibly touched and changed – not just claims and public fervour
Yes. A discovery so great cannot leave a person unmoved.
questions.rationale: “They display religious fervour in public, but there are no signs of their souls being illuminated with the light of God.”

questions.article: Why Has God Given Man Freedom?
questions.q: Stars, rivers and animals follow God’s will without choice. Why has man alone been given freedom?
options: So that he may rule over other creatures
Not quite. The article says: So that he may choose to live uprightly without compulsion, and so earn the highest credit.
So that he may live as he pleases
Not quite. The article says: So that he may choose to live uprightly without compulsion, and so earn the highest credit.
So that he need answer to no one
Not quite. The article says: So that he may choose to live uprightly without compulsion, and so earn the highest credit.
So that he may choose to live uprightly without compulsion, and so earn the highest credit
Exactly. The freedom is a test.
questions.rationale: “Its purpose is that man should lead a morally upright life of his own free will… without being subjected to any external force.”

questions.article: Where All Hopes End, New Hope Emerges
questions.q: Roosevelt wrote, “The light has gone out of my life,” and later became President. What does the article say explains such recoveries?
options: Powerful friends come to the rescue
Not quite. The article says: An outer loss awakens the mind and will, which are greater than what was lost.
An outer loss awakens the mind and will, which are greater than what was lost
Well read. “The power of construction is stronger than the power of destruction.”
Time heals every wound by itself
Not quite. The article says: An outer loss awakens the mind and will, which are greater than what was lost.
Loss is usually smaller than it seems
Not quite. The article says: An outer loss awakens the mind and will, which are greater than what was lost.
questions.rationale: “What he has inside him is far greater than what he has lost outside of him… every external loss further activates the inner asset of a person, which is his mind.”
